tool.name: bcftools @EXECUTABLE@
tool.description: Extracts fields from VCF/BCF file and prints them in user-defined format

param.name: force_samples
param.label: Force Samples
param.help: Only warn about unknown subset samples

param.name: format
param.label: Format for Output
param.help: Example: %CHROM\t%POS\t%REF\t%ALT{0}\n ( NOTE TAB: '\t' and new line character: '\n' )

param.name: tsv
param.label: Output is tab-delimited
param.help: Fields in your Format are separated by a TAB character: \t

param.name: disable_automatic_newline
param.label: Disable automatic newline
param.help: Disable automatic addition of newline character when not present in the formatting expression (-N)

param.name: print_filtered
param.label: Print Filtered
param.help: Output string for samples failing the -i/-e filtering expression (-F)

tool.help:
===================================== bcftools @EXECUTABLE@ =====================================
Extracts fields from VCF/BCF file and prints them in user-defined format
Format:
::
``%CHROM`` The CHROM column (similarly also other columns: POS, ID, REF, ALT, QUAL, FILTER) ``%INFO`` Prints the whole INFO column ``%INFO/TAG`` Any tag in the INFO column ``%TYPE`` Variant type (REF, SNP, MNP, INDEL, OTHER) ``%MASK`` Indicates presence of the site in other files (with multiple files) ``%TAG{INT}`` Curly brackets to subscript vectors (0-based) ``%FIRST_ALT`` Alias for %ALT{0} ``[]`` The brackets loop over all samples ``%GT`` Genotype (e.g. 0/1) ``%TBCSQ`` Translated FORMAT/BCSQ. See the csq command above for explanation and examples. ``%TGT`` Translated genotype (e.g. C/A) ``%IUPACGT`` Genotype translated to IUPAC ambiguity codes (e.g. M instead of C/A) ``%FORMAT`` Prints all FORMAT fields or a subset of samples with -s or -S ``%FUNCTION`` Functions supported by the -i/-e filtering expressions (e.g. "[ %sSUM(FMT/AD)] %SUM(FMT/AD) %SUM(INFO/AD)") ``%N_PASS(expr)`` Number of samples that pass the filtering expression (see *<<expressions,EXPRESSIONS>>*) ``%PBINOM(TAG)`` Calculate phred-scaled binomial probability, the allele index is determined from GT ``%VKX`` VariantKey, biallelic hexadecimal encoding of CHROM,POS,REF,ALT (https://github.com/tecnickcom/variantkey) ``%LINE`` Prints the whole line ``%SAMPLE`` Sample name ``%POS0`` POS in 0-based coordinates ``%END`` End position of the REF allele ``%END0`` End position of the REF allele in 0-based cordinates ``\n`` new line, adds automatically unless disabled ``\t`` tab character
Examples:
::
# Print chromosome, position, ref allele and the first alternate allele bcftools query -f '%CHROM %POS %REF %ALT{0}\n' file.vcf.gz
# Similar to above, but use tabs instead of spaces, add sample name and genotype bcftools query -f '%CHROM\t%POS\t%REF\t%ALT[\t%SAMPLE=%GT]\n' file.vcf.gz
# Print FORMAT/GT fields followed by FORMAT/GT fields bcftools query -f 'GQ:[ %GQ] \t GT:[ %GT]\n' file.vcf
# Make a BED file: chr, pos (0-based), end pos (1-based), id bcftools query -f'%CHROM\t%POS0\t%END\t%ID\n' file.bcf
# Print only samples with alternate (non-reference) genotypes bcftools query -f'[%CHROM:%POS %SAMPLE %GT\n]' -i'GT="alt"' file.bcf
# Print all samples at sites with at least one alternate genotype bcftools view -i'GT="alt"' file.bcf -Ou | bcftools query -f'[%CHROM:%POS %SAMPLE %GT\n]'
# Print phred-scaled binomial probability from FORMAT/AD tag for all heterozygous genotypes bcftools query -i'GT="het"' -f'[%CHROM:%POS %SAMPLE %GT %PBINOM(AD)\n]' file.vcf
# Print the second value of AC field if bigger than 10. Note the (unfortunate) difference in # index subscript notation: formatting expressions (-f) uses "{}" while filtering expressions # (-i) use "[]". This is for historic reasons and backward-compatibility. bcftools query -f '%AC{1}\n' -i 'AC[1]>10' file.vcf.gz
# Print all samples at sites where at least one sample has DP=1 or DP=2. In the second case # print only samples with DP=1 or DP=2, the difference is in the logical operator used, || vs |. bcftools query -f '[%SAMPLE %GT %DP\n]' -i 'FMT/DP=1 || FMT/DP=2' file.vcf bcftools query -f '[%SAMPLE %GT %DP\n]' -i 'FMT/DP=1 | FMT/DP=2' file.vcf
# Refer to ID column vs INFO/ID tag vs FORMAT/ID tag bcftools query -f 'columnID=%ID infoID=%INFO/ID [fmtID=%ID ] [columnID=%/ID]'
